kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
wire.summary: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

wire.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
wire.summary: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?

wire.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
wire.summary: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

wire.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
wire.summary: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

wire.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
wire.summary: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?

wire.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
wire.summary: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.

wire.title: Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70 percent of websites
wire.summary: Governments around the world are rushing to implement safety measures after AI technology found 'severe' vulnerabilities in a key programming language called PHP.

wire.title: Amid Trump's assaults on DEI, how one university is elevating Black students
wire.summary: As many colleges roll back or eliminate such programs, Sacramento State has expanded its offerings for students of color.

wire.title: Gen Z is 'in the thick' of high housing costs. These candidates aim to solve it
wire.summary: Young candidates who rent or live with parents say their generation is "in the thick" of the country's housing affordability crisis. They argue this gives them new energy to solve it for everyone.

wire.title: After nearly 6 years, ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi's son hears her voice
wire.summary: Kim Aris tells NPR his mother sounds strong but is in pain. He says she is held at a residence in the capital.

wire.title: Deadly shooting near Paris investigated as 'crime of terrorism', minister says
wire.summary: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks and the suspected gunman has been apprehended.

wire.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
wire.summary: Thirty-four people are also injured in the attack in southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.

wire.title: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
wire.summary: The soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint outside the West Bank city on Friday morning.

wire.title: White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
wire.summary: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.

wire.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
wire.summary: The network is used by the Ukrainian military, sources say, and Trump says "if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out".

wire.title: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
wire.summary: Satellite images show oil spreading for miles along the coastline, threatening local marine wildlife
